body:
You are the most notorious criminal in Gwalior. You've decided that you're going to rob hard working employees of CF, a famous Tech company in the city.

There are N people working in CF. The employees working here are conveniently numbered from 1 to N. Furthermore, each employee except Praveen, the CEO, has exactly 1 manager that he/she has to report to regularly. We denote the manager of the ith employee as Mi. Mi = 0 denotes that the ith employee is the CEO(Praveen). Each employee also has a salary (in rupees), which is denoted by Si. We also define another term, SUBi, which denotes the set of employees that are subordinates of the ith employee. An employee y is a subordinate of x iff x = My or My is a subordinate of x. Note that all employees (except the CEO) are subordinates of the CEO.

Since CF hires only from top institutions, the employees there are really smart. Whenever you rob an employee x, x tells his/her manager Mx about the incident. Mx in turn, tells MMx about the incident, and this goes on until the CEO hears about it. Also, all subordinates of x i.e. all employees in SUBx hear about the incident. Upon hearing about the incident, these employees start taking extra precautions and thus you cannot rob them in the future. Obviously, x takes extra precautions as well to avoid getting robbed again. Robbing employee x gives you Sx rupees.

You want to maximize the amount of money you can earn by robbing exactly K employees. Given information about this company, can you find the optimal amount?

Input

The first line of input contains an integer T denoting the number of test cases. The description of T test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two space separated integers N and K.

The next N lines of each test case contains 2 space separated integers each. The ith line contains two space separated integers, Mi and Si.

Output

For each test case, output a single line containing the answer. If a valid subset of K employees does not exist, print -1.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ T ≤ 2000
  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ K ≤ 103
  • 0 ≤ Mi ≤ N
  • 1 ≤ Si ≤ 2000
  • Sum of NK in a single test file does not exceed 108

Example

Input:
2
4 2
0 2
1 5
2 1
1 3
3 3
0 100
1 5
1 3

Output:
8
-1

Explanation


The picture above represents the first test case. In this case, you rob employee 2 first. This notifies employees 1 and 3 about the incident. Next, you rob employee 4 earning a total of 5 + 3 = 8 dollars.

In the second case, you cannot rob all three employees without getting caught.

All submissions for this problem are available.

problemComponents.statement:
You are the most notorious criminal in **Gwalior**. You've decided that you're going to rob hard working employees of **CF**, a famous Tech company in the city.

There are **N** people working in **CF**. The employees working here are conveniently numbered from **1** to **N**. Furthermore, each employee except **Praveen**, the **CEO**, has exactly **1** manager that he/she has to report to regularly. We denote the manager of the **ith** employee as **$M_i$**. **$M_i = 0$** denotes that the **ith** employee is the CEO (Praveen). Each employee also has a salary (in rupees), which is denoted by **$S_i$**. We also define another term, **$SUB_i$**, which denotes the set of employees that are subordinates of the **ith** employee. An employee **y** is a subordinate of **x** iff **$x = M_y$** or **$M_y$** is a subordinate of **x**. Note that all employees (except the CEO) are subordinates of the CEO.

Since **CF** hires only from top institutions, the employees there are really smart. Whenever you rob an employee **x**, **x** tells his/her manager **$M_x$** about the incident. **$M_x$** in turn, tells **$M_{M_x}$** about the incident, and this goes on until the CEO hears about it. Also, all subordinates of **x** i.e. all employees in **$SUB_x$** hear about the incident. Upon hearing about the incident, these employees start taking extra precautions and thus you cannot rob them in the future. Obviously, **x** takes extra precautions as well to avoid getting robbed again. Robbing employee **x** gives you **$S_x$** rupees.

You want to maximize the amount of money you can earn by robbing **exactly K** employees. Given information about this company, can you find the optimal amount?
